facts.truth: In GL one row is one journal line; lines sharing a Txn # form one balanced transaction (594 transactions, 1419 lines).

Credits are exported as positive numbers through 2025-03-31 (old desktop books, GJ- numbers) and as negative numbers from 2025-04-01 (new cloud ledger, T25- numbers). Both are credits; net for an account is Debit minus the absolute Credit.
The COA tab maps each account to Bank, Fixed Asset, Credit Card, Liability, Equity, Income, COGS or Expense.
Transfers between 1000 Operating Checking and 1010 Savings (14 of them) and Tern Card payments (debit 2100) are money moving between the business's own accounts, not expenses.
Account 3100 Owner Draws holds Dana Whitfield's personal draws; it is equity and must be excluded from expenses.

Account 9999 Ask My Accountant is a suspense account for unclassified bank feed items (8 lines, $12,872.39 debit balance). It is deliberately missing from the COA and belongs in no P&L total until reclassified.

The 2025-08-14 WIRE OUT of $8,750.00 in 9999 is the deposit on the new deck oven (Brightforge Ovens) and belongs in 1500 Equipment; the 2025-04-22 $1,200 mobile deposit is a catering deposit from Marlow & Finch LLP and belongs in 4100.
Vendor refunds are credits to the original COGS or expense account (memo starts "Refund:"); customer refunds are debits to 4100 Catering Sales.
Class Downtown and Lakewood are the two shops, Catering is the catering business, blank means shared overhead.
Deposits include 7% sales tax booked to 2200 Sales Tax Payable and remitted monthly on the 20th; it is not revenue.
The first transaction (2025-01-01) is the opening balance entry; the GL covers calendar 2025 only.
The bookkeeper wants 2025 closed for the CPA: suspense cleared, a P&L by class, and draws kept out of expenses.

owner_brief:
You are Rosa Delgado, the part-time bookkeeper for Heron & Hearth Bakery, owned by Dana Whitfield. The bakery has two shops, Downtown and Lakewood, and a small catering business. You exported ledger_gl.xlsx for calendar 2025: the GL tab is every journal line and the COA tab is the chart of accounts.

The export: on April 1, 2025 the bakery moved from old desktop accounting software to a cloud ledger. The old software exported credits as positive numbers in the Credit column; the new one exports them as negative numbers. Both mean a credit. Transaction numbers changed too: GJ- before April, T25- after. The first entry, on January 1, is the opening balances.

Classes: Downtown and Lakewood are the shops, Catering is catering; a blank class is shared overhead.

Not expenses: transfers between Operating Checking and Savings, payments on the Tern Card (the expenses were booked when they were charged), and Dana's owner draws in 3100, which are equity. Sales tax (7%) goes to 2200 and is paid to the state on the 20th of each month; it is not revenue.

Refunds: vendor refunds are credited back to the account the expense was booked to, with a memo starting "Refund:". Catering cancellations are refunded as debits to Catering Sales.

Suspense: 9999 Ask My Accountant is where bank feed items go when you cannot classify them. It is not in the COA on purpose because it is supposed to be temporary. You know two of them: the August 14 wire of $8,750 is the deposit on the new deck oven from Brightforge Ovens and belongs in 1500 Equipment; the April 22 mobile deposit of $1,200 is a catering deposit from Marlow & Finch LLP and belongs in 4100. You do not know what the others are.

Your goal: close 2025 for the CPA with suspense cleaned up, a P&L by class, and draws kept out of expenses.

Answer only what you are asked, briefly. If a question is not covered here, say "not sure".

eval_questions.q: What were total operating expenses in 2025 (Expense accounts only, net of refunds)?
eval_questions.a: $672,620.00. Credits count as reductions whatever their sign in the export; transfers, card payments, draws and suspense are not expenses.

eval_questions.a: $70,000.00 in 14 draws to Dana Whitfield (account 3100, equity, not an expense).

eval_questions.a: 14 transfers; net $11,000.00 into Savings. They are neither income nor expense.

eval_questions.q: What is the year-end balance in account 9999, and how many lines post to it?
eval_questions.a: $12,872.39 debit balance across 8 lines. 9999 is a suspense account for bank feed items not yet classified.

eval_questions.q: Which account numbers in the GL are missing from the COA tab?

eval_questions.a: Catering $90,122.01; Downtown $562,744.23; Lakewood $388,967.12. Sales tax collected is a liability, not revenue.

eval_questions.q: What is the Operating Checking (1000) balance at December 31, 2025?
eval_questions.a: $108,308.60, including the January 1 opening balance. Adding the raw Credit column instead of treating every credit as a reduction gives a wrong number.

eval_questions.q: How much came back from vendors as refunds in 2025?
eval_questions.a: $1,844.75 over 8 refunds, booked as credits to the original COGS or expense accounts.

eval_questions.q: Which expense account was largest in 2025, and how much?
How are credits signed in the Credit column, and does that change during the year?
eval_questions.a: Credits are positive through 2025-03-31 (old desktop books, GJ- numbers) and negative from 2025-04-01 (new cloud ledger, T25- numbers). Both mean a credit: net = Debit minus the absolute Credit.

eval_questions.q: What is the largest item sitting in suspense 9999, and where does it belong?
eval_questions.a: The 2025-08-14 wire of $8,750.00 (memo WIRE OUT) is the deposit on the new deck oven from Brightforge Ovens; it belongs in 1500 Equipment, not an expense.
